title: Vermicelli
description:
Vermicelli is a versatile, thin pasta-like ingredient widely used in Indian cuisine for both sweet and savory dishes, available in wheat, rice, and millet varieties.

Types of Vermicelli

In India, vermicelli comes in several types based on the main ingredient:

  • Wheat-Semolina Vermicelli: The most common type, rich in fiber and protein, suitable for dishes like upma and kheer aashirvaad.com.

  • Rice Vermicelli: Often used in savory dishes like rice sevai or stir-fried pulao, it is light and gluten-free bigbasket.

  • Millet Vermicelli: Made from millets such as ragi, little millet, or barnyard millet, it is highly nutritious and a healthier alternative to refined flour vermicelli aashirvaad.com+1.

  • Refined Flour (Maida) Vermicelli: Less healthy due to low nutritional value, but occasionally used in traditional recipes aashirvaad.com.
    Vermicelli is available in roasted and unroasted forms, with roasted vermicelli often preferred for better flavor and texture
